title: Batchshape constraint enforcer and quantization rollback guard
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Motivation: customers with bursty and heterogeneous request shapes were hitting degraded unit economics when aggressive quantization + microbatch shapes combined with prefix caching led to increased token counts and unexpected latency spikes. This PR introduces a lightweight batchshape constraint enforcer that injects shape-aware fallbacks and a quantization rollback guard that can trigger safe fallbacks to higher-precision model variants when latency or quality regressions are observed.

What this change does: adds a new runtime policy component (BatchshapeConstraintEnforcer) that evaluates incoming aggregate batch shapes against tenant-configured constraints and enforces one of: (a) soften batching (reduce microbatch coalescing), (b) route to warm-prepared shard, or (c) fallback to a conservative quant profile. In addition the QuantRollbackGuard observes short-window latency/quality signals and will atomically switch model variant to a pinned higher-precision variant for the in-flight tenant for a configurable cooldown. Both pieces are opt-in via tenant defaults and a CLI to generate safe profiles.

Why this approach: previous attempts to just tighten quant thresholds caused regressions for complex prompt families. By making the guard runtime-aware and tenant-scoped we can preserve aggressive cost savings for well-behaved workloads while protecting SLAs for edge case tenants. The design keeps the control plane minimal and leverages existing routing and cache snapshots.

Checklist:
- [x] add runtime enforcer and unit tests
- [x] add integration test that simulates bursty shapes + cold KV cache
- [x] add CLI to export safe rollback profiles (prefill-suggest)
- [x] add telemetry/alerts for rollback events and affected token delta
- [x] update docs and SDK surface (python/ts) with opt-in flags

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the decision heuristics conservative; a follow-up will add an offline tuner to recommend tenant constraints from historical traces. Related: ENG-712 (prefill/workload-profiling), PM-88 (tenant SLA strategy).

release_notes: Adds a runtime batchshape constraint enforcer and a quantization rollback guard to protect latency/quality during aggressive cost optimization. Opt-in via tenant defaults; includes new telemetry and CLI helpers to export safe rollback profiles.
notes_for_release: Disabled by default. Recommend enabling for tenants with >95th percentile variability in sequence shapes after running costctl analyze-prefill. Ops runbook included in docs/operations/batchshape-rollback.md.
qa_summary: Integration harness simulates 10 tenants with mixed shapes and KV-cold states; verified no token inflation regressions and <1.5% end-to-end latency delta for protected tenants. Rollback events are emitted and can be correlated with failing quality assertions in synthetic evals.
